Who developed Python?
actual: Python was created by Guido van Rossum. He began developing it in December 1989 at the Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) in the Netherlands, and released the first public version (0.9.0) in 1991. Van Rossum led the project (often called the BDFL) until he stepped down in 2018. Today Python is developed and maintained by a large open-source community and organizations such as the Python Software Foundation; the reference implementation is CPython.
